## Header 1

```{r setup}
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(snakecase)

source(here("R/functions.R"))
```

## Importing raw data

First we need to import the csv data. Use the package readr that is part of tidyverse

here() is my project location ("/home/ztml/LearnR3"). If I move the project to another PC. I don't have to rewrite everytime I have used a path.

I add show_col_types = F for avoid innecessary output regarding the delimiter of the csv file. 

```{r}
here("data-raw/nurses-stress/stress/5C/5C_1586886626/HR.csv.gz") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE)
```

Notice that the collumn names are in PascalCase (no spaces, uppercase...). We want snake_case.We use the function to_snake_case() from the snakecase package, as an argument for name_repair

I add n_max for the future data that I will import, that might be big and I don't want to load it all when I am only playing with the data.

```{r}
here("data-raw/nurses-stress/stress/5C/5C_1586886626/HR.csv.gz") |>
  read_csv(
    show_col_types = FALSE,
    name_repair = to_snake_case,
    n_max = 100
  )
```

## Import 5C's HR data with a function

```{r}
read <- function(file_path) {
  data <- file_path |>
    read_csv(
      show_col_types = FALSE,
      name_repair = to_snake_case,
      n_max = 100
    )
  return(data)
}
```

Now to test it:

```{r}
here("data-raw/nurses-stress/stress/5C/5C_1586886626/HR.csv.gz") |>
  read()
```
Now adding Roxygen documentation:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#' read()
#' Opens a file from a path, snake_cases columns. Max rows: 100
#' @param file_path Path to the data file
#'
#' @returns Outputs a data frame
#'

read <- function(file_path) {
  data <- file_path |>
    read_csv(
      show_col_types = FALSE,
      name_repair = to_snake_case,
      n_max = 100
    )
  return(data)
}
```

```{r}
here("data-raw/nurses-stress/stress/5C/5C_1586886712/HR.csv.gz") |>
  read()
```

## Making function reusable

When someone needs one of our functions, they need to have installed the packages we are using. We add these packages in the DESCRIPTION file. Using the following lines:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
usethis::use_package("here")
usethis::use_package("tidyverse", type = "Depends") # requires to add it to depends otherwise gives an error
```

Good practice is to add before the function, the package where it comes from + ::. Then I can remove it from the setup chunk library()

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#' Read in one nurses' stress data file
#'
#' @param file_path Path to the data file
#' @param max_rows Maximum numbers of rows to read
#'
#' @returns Outputs a data frame/tibble
#' 
read <- function(file_path, max_rows = 100) {
  data <- file_path |>
    readr::read_csv(
      show_col_types = FALSE,
      name_repair = snakecase::to_snake_case,
      n_max = max_rows
    )
  return(data)
}
```

Adding more packages to the description

```{r, eval=FALSE}
usethis::use_package("readr")
usethis::use_package("snakecase")
```

Good practice is to move the function to the functions.R file once it works. And delete it from the markdown so that it doesn't become long
